This skill doesn't apply to your offering.

**Why:** You're running pure SaaS — software is already modular by nature (features, seats, usage limits, integrations). The atomic-decomposition logic in this skill is built for *service* offerings, where the deliverables are human time, expertise, and artifacts that need to be broken apart and reconfigured. Your product is already broken apart; the work you're describing is **packaging and pricing**, not productization.

**What you likely want instead:**

- **SaaS pricing/packaging frameworks** — value-metric selection (per seat vs. per project vs. per usage), feature-gating logic across Free/Pro/Enterprise, and good/better/best tier construction. Kyle Poyar (OpenView) and Patrick Campbell (ProfitWell) are the canonical references.
- **Feature-tier mapping** — deciding which features anchor each plan, which drive upgrades, and which create Enterprise-only differentiation.
- **Expansion-revenue design** — usage-based add-ons, seat expansion mechanics, and Enterprise-plan variable components.
- **PLG motion design** — if the question is really "how does freemium convert to Pro to Enterprise."

**One edge case where this skill *would* apply:** if alongside the SaaS you sell (or want to sell) **services** — onboarding packages, implementation, custom integrations, training, CSM tiers, migration services. Those are clay. The software isn't.

If that's actually what you're after — productizing the services that wrap the SaaS — re-prompt with that scope and I'll run the blueprint.

This skill doesn't apply here.

Modularizing a physical product is a different problem: SKU variants, bundles, and configurators (material, color, monogramming, card-slot count, etc.).

What you likely want instead:

- **SKU/variant architecture** — base wallet + axes of variation (leather type, thread color, edge finish, card slots, monogram)

- **Made-to-order configurator** — customer picks options, price calculated from variant matrix

If you want to go down that path, I'd point you at an e-commerce / product-line skill, not this one.

### Tier 1 — **Clay Open** (Free / MIT)
- **Configuration:** Self-serve depth · Single offering · One-shot · OSS file only · Community support · No add-ons · No vertical pack · 0 operator hours
- **Positioning:** For the solo operator who wants to productize one offering themselves using Claude Code. Read the repo, install the skill, run it, ship.

### Tier 2 — **Clay Pro** *(flagship)* — `+$B/year` or `+$B one-time`
- **Configuration:** Reviewed depth · Single vertical · Ongoing async · Hosted + UI · Email 48hr support · Configurator export + Memory adapter + 1 Vertical Pack · 1hr operator hours
- **Positioning:** For the established consultant or boutique agency who's productizing seriously and wants vertical benchmarks, a configurator they can embed in their site, and a human to sanity-check the output.
- **Pricing logic:** Anchored against the cost of one botched productization attempt (typically 20–40 hours of founder time + a wrong-priced launch). Priced so the BYO sum of {Vertical Pack + Configurator export + Memory adapter + 1hr operator + hosted UI} comes out ~25–35% higher than flagship.

### Tier 3 — **Clay Studio** — `+$C/year` retainer
- **Configuration:** Co-produced depth · Multi-vertical team · Quarterly tune-up · Embedded in their stack · Slack Connect + Dedicated operator · All add-ons (all vertical packs, configurator export, memory adapter, self-iteration Action, team seats) · 10hr+ operator hours/quarter
- **Positioning:** For agencies and consultancies with 3+ productized service lines who want Clay embedded in their internal tooling and a maintainer on call to re-blueprint as offerings evolve.
- **Pricing logic:** Anchored against the cost of hiring a fractional product strategist (typically $4–8K/month). Studio comes in below that with the IP advantage of the skill maintainer.
